# hookbase_source (Resource)

Manages a Hookbase inbound webhook source.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Basic Stripe webhook source
resource "hookbase_source" "stripe" {
  name          = "stripe-production"
  slug          = "stripe-prod"
  provider_type = "stripe"
  signing_secret = var.stripe_webhook_secret
  reject_invalid_signatures = true
}

# GitHub source with IP filtering
resource "hookbase_source" "github" {
  name           = "github-webhooks"
  slug           = "github"
  provider_type  = "github"
  ip_filter_mode = "allowlist"
  ip_allowlist   = ["140.82.112.0/20", "185.199.108.0/22"]
}

# High-security source with deduplication and transient mode
resource "hookbase_source" "payments" {
  name               = "payment-events"
  slug               = "payments"
  provider_type      = "custom"
  dedup_enabled      = true
  dedup_strategy     = "idempotency_key"
  dedup_window_hours = 48
  transient_mode     = true  # HIPAA compliance — no payload storage
}

# Source restricted to specific HTTP methods (omit allowed_methods to accept any verb)
resource "hookbase_source" "poller" {
  name            = "status-poller"
  slug            = "status-poller"
  provider_type   = "generic"
  allowed_methods = ["GET", "HEAD"]
}

# WhatsApp source: Hookbase generates the Meta "Verify token" unless verify_token is set.
# signing_secret is the Meta App Secret, which Meta issues.
resource "hookbase_source" "whatsapp" {
  name           = "whatsapp"
  slug           = "whatsapp"
  provider_type  = "whatsapp"
  signing_secret = var.meta_app_secret
}

output "whatsapp_verify_token" {
  value     = hookbase_source.whatsapp.verify_token
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Source name (1-100 characters).
- `slug` (String) URL-safe identifier. Lowercase alphanumeric and hyphens only. Changing this forces a new resource.

### Optional

- `allowed_methods` (List of String) HTTP methods the ingest endpoint accepts: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD. Omit or set to an empty list to accept any method.
- `dedup_custom_header` (String) Custom header name for idempotency key dedup strategy.
- `dedup_enabled` (Boolean) Enable event deduplication.
- `dedup_strategy` (String) Deduplication strategy: auto, provider_id, payload_hash, idempotency_key, or none.
- `dedup_window_hours` (Number) Deduplication window in hours (1-168).
- `description` (String) Source description.
- `encrypt_fields` (List of String) Field names to encrypt.
- `ip_allowlist` (List of String) IP addresses or CIDR ranges to allow.
- `ip_denylist` (List of String) IP addresses or CIDR ranges to deny.
- `ip_filter_mode` (String) IP filtering mode: none, allowlist, denylist, or both.
- `is_active` (Boolean) Whether the source is active.
- `mask_fields` (List of String) Field names to mask in the UI.
- `provider_type` (String) Webhook provider, which selects the signature scheme used to verify incoming requests. The value is the integration's provider id, as shown for each integration at https://www.hookbase.app/integrations (for example github, stripe or standard-webhooks). Omit for a source that accepts unsigned requests. The API validates the value, so an unsupported provider fails at apply with the API's error. Changing it updates the source in place; switching to a provider whose secret the vendor issues needs signing_secret set in the same change.
- `rate_limit_per_minute` (Number) Rate limit per minute (1-100000). Requires paid plan.
- `reject_invalid_signatures` (Boolean) Reject webhooks with invalid signatures.
- `signing_secret` (String, Sensitive) Webhook signing secret, or for public-key providers the vendor's public key. Whether to set it depends on the provider (see each integration at https://www.hookbase.app/integrations): for providers where Hookbase issues the secret (e.g. github, gitlab, bitbucket, typeform, or no provider) leave it unset and Hookbase generates one, which is stored in state at create so you can paste it into the vendor; for providers where the vendor issues the secret or public key (e.g. stripe, shopify, slack, standard-webhooks/svix, airtable, gitlab-signing-token, discord, sendgrid) copy it from the vendor — public keys and format-checked keys (standard-webhooks/svix, airtable, gitlab-signing-token) are rejected without it, and the rest are created with no secret (awaiting_signing_secret is true, events unverified) until it is set; asana and notion issue it only after the ingest URL is registered, so leave it unset at create (awaiting_signing_secret is true) and set it once received; wise, wise-sandbox and aws-sns verify against keys the vendor publishes, so it must be omitted (verifies_without_secret is true). Null in state when the source has no secret. Removing it from configuration leaves the stored secret unchanged.
- `transient_mode` (Boolean) Discard payloads after routing (HIPAA/GDPR compliance).
- `verify_token` (String, Sensitive) Meta "Verify token" for WhatsApp sources (provider_type = "whatsapp" only; the API rejects it for any other provider). Copy it into Meta's webhook "Verify token" field. Generated by Hookbase if not set (8-256 visible ASCII characters when set). Null for providers without one.

### Read-Only

- `awaiting_signing_secret` (Boolean) True when no secret is set and only the vendor can issue one (e.g. stripe or shopify created without signing_secret, or asana/notion, which issue it only after the ingest URL is registered); events are accepted unverified until it is set.
- `created_at` (String) Creation timestamp.
- `has_signing_secret` (Boolean) Whether a signing secret is stored for this source.
- `id` (String) Source ID.
- `ingest_url` (String) The public URL for sending webhooks to this source.
- `updated_at` (String) Last update timestamp.
- `verifies_without_secret` (Boolean) True when the provider signs with a key it publishes (wise, wise-sandbox, aws-sns), so no signing secret is stored or needed.
